newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares slips but morale high - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares slips but morale high - brokers.

text.p: Egyptian share prices retreated on Thursday but brokers believed the bourse would again ride an upward wave after foreign investors and newly established mutual funds start filling their portfolios.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index shed 1.16 points to close at 380.8 points in above-average turnover of 58.8 million pounds ($17.3 million).
"Foreign investors started buying after a wait-and-see stand to make sure that prices have reached the bottom of the correction," said Dalia Sultan of brokers EFG/Hermes.

"American Express has also started operation," she told Reuters in reference to the bank's new fund which closed on April 1. The fund increased its value to 300 million pounds from its initial 100 million.
"Prices will surely go up as several new funds will start operation soon,"said Hany Hosny of Megavest.
The brokers said the cement sector would most likely benefit the most from the increasing demand. "Cement firms are in large demand by Amex and foreign investors,"said Sultan.
The most active stock of the day was Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA, but it closed 0.40 pounds down at 77.6 after shares worth 9.7 million pounds changed hands.

Egyptian Tora Portland Cement was the second most active cement share, when 4.86 million pounds worth of shares were traded. It fell only 0.01 to close at 97.49. Amriyah Cement was also active and gained 0.80 pounds to close at 85.30 pounds.
Banks, with the exception of Commercial International Bank (CIB) COMIq.LT, lost their attraction for investors who limited their trading to a handful of stocks from last week's heavy turnover.
CIB was the second most active share across the board, with stocks worth 8.13 million pounds trading. But the share ended 2.5 pounds down at 79.00.
Misr International Bank/MIBank regained Wednesday's loss, rising 5.00 pounds to end at 760.00. MIBank is taking preparations for a GDR issue.
In the favourite milling sector, North Cairo Flour Mills was the most active, gaining 5.00 pounds to 190.00.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills, one of three in which the state now holds less than 50 percent, ended 1.64 pounds down at 90.61 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 585.62 points from 595.56 points on Wednesday. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 264.32 from 262.93 points.
Out of the 87 shares traded on Thursday, 41 gained, 26 lost and 20 ended unchanged.
